QUESTION THIS VIEW ANSWERS
What expense and discount losses must the plan recover?

Venue contribution per additional guest

How much contribution would the venue retain per additional guest under each offer?

Venue contribution per additional guest

USD cents retained by the venue per additional guest after the offer and variable costs. Additional means a visit caused by the promotion; returning customers can count. A visit attributed to an offer is not necessarily additional. Unknown remains unknown; zero or negative contribution cannot cover a positive cost. Break-even counts cover the plan’s additional expense plus any separate existing-customer discount loss.

Separate discount loss on existing customers

Would an offer reduce contribution from guests who would have come anyway?

Separate discount loss on existing customers

USD cents of additional contribution lost on guests who would have attended anyway. Include only loss not already counted in guest contribution or the plan’s expense. Break-even counts cover additional expense plus this separate loss. Unknown leaves the guest target unassessed.

checks: The frozen local production runtime and startup settings match their retained hashes; no public-deployment parity is claimed.
The 1.3 starter has no calculations or reviews. No reviewer identity, acting-role, answer-state or acceptance controls appear.

Applying two callouts and Calculate establishes holding and the one-person plan, plus the $200/$40/five/six hurdle. Navigation and Forms/YAML switching retain an unapplied draft without changing the native saved run.

Applying the third callout makes the previous calculation stale. Recalculate creates a current, complete calculation with only holding feasible. Exactly one staffing field changes; definition and all other case facts remain unchanged, and there are no review records.
Inspecting the financial supporting report preserves the original five-staff native run. Excel starts collapsed; inspection grants no authority and records no deployment choice.
